notes:
195 stations: 4 + 27 + 36 + 35 + 4 + 44 + 40 + 5. These match the counts given. Order: each section's left column first, then its right column. Scotland E. (4–29) comes before England E. (30–65), and Scotland W. and the Isle of Man (81–118) come before England W. (119–162). Ireland 1–19 comes before 20–40. Line numbers for right-column rows are the lines those rows are printed on, so they overlap the left column's.

Format of this list: it gives only map numbers, names and types. There are no keepers, no return marks (*, † etc.) and no light characters. So keepers is [] and character is null throughout. The only printed mark is the brace "{" on lines 148–149, joining 11 Hoy Sound (Low) and 12 Hoy Sound (High) as one pair of lights. "_b_" in 3_b_, 28_b_ and 109_b_ is an italic letter in the number, not an italic name. In Ireland 5* and 8* the asterisk belongs to the number, so marks is null there.

Choices I made:
- I dropped the list's closing full stop from names and types (e.g. "Iceland.", "Lt.-ship."). I did the same with the trailing commas after "Hoy Sound (High)," (line 149) and "Heligoland," (line 247), which look like slips for full stops. The fragments keep all of these exactly.
- Line 228, "5*.Coningbeg. Lt.-ship.": there is a stray full stop after Coningbeg and no space after "5*." (same for "8*.Arklow N.").
- Line 135, "2. Do.": "Do." means ditto, a second station in Iceland (presumably). I kept it as the name.
- Numbers 1–3b have no coast heading, so coast is null for them. The other reader called them "N. outliers".
- The England--West Coast heading (line 173) is missing its closing "=", so it is printed "=England--West Coast.".
- The dates "(1885)" for Fidra and "(1880)" for Langness, and "(building, 1885)" for Ailsa Craig, are in other.
- In "Fladda, Easdale", "Pladda, Arran", "Old Head, Kinsale", "Blackrock, Mayo", "Skerryvore and Hynish Signal Tower, Tiree" and the outlying stations, I took the words after the comma as the place. Splitting "Old Head, Kinsale" is debatable: the headland is usually called "Old Head of Kinsale". In "Eagle Island, E.", "Slyne Head, N." and similar, the E./W./N./S. stays in the name.

Scottish, Manx and Irish stations mostly have no L.H./L.V. type. The Irish light-vessels are "Lt.-ship".

Spellings as printed that you may want to standardise later (none corrected):
- England: "Llyn Wells" (= Lynn Well L.V.), "Languard Point" (Landguard), "Air L.H." (Point of Ayr), "Great Castlehead" (Great Castle Head), "Wolf-Rock".
- Scotland: "Montroseness" (= Scurdy Ness, Montrose), "Island Ghlais" (Eilean Glas), "Rhinns of May" (almost certainly a misprint for Rhinns of Islay, as it sits between Skervuile and Lochindaul), "N Ronaldshay" (no stop after N), "Whalsey".
- Ireland: "Arran Island" (= Aran Islands, Ireland), "Innishtrahull".

Unused numbers: 66–80 in the main list, and 9 and 35 in Ireland.
